set.typical_award_size: State density bonus law implemented in Chapter 17.12 (last amended Ordinance 5286, 2018) with a County enhanced density bonus (Section 17.12.065) in lieu of the regular 35% state bonus, capped at a resulting density of 30 units per acre: at least 21% low income units earns 36.5%, rising 1.5 points per percentage point to 50% at 30%; at least 12% very low income units earns 37.5%, rising 2.5 points to 50% at 17%; at least 15% moderate income units (including on-site inclusionary units) earns 40%, rising 1 point to 50% at 25%; and 100% affordable projects (all rental units very low or low income, or all for-sale units low or moderate) earn a 75% enhanced bonus when the sponsor or site owner is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit or public agency and the project uses public subsidy, tax credits or publicly provided land, with 55-year rental and 45-year for-sale restrictions. Incentives: one, two or three concessions at 10%, 20% or 30% lower income (5%, 10%, 15% very low income); priority processing under Section 17.10.040 is a listed concession.
set.affordability_requirement: Government Code 65915 thresholds (5% very low, 10% low, senior, moderate for-sale) with 55-year recorded restrictions; enhanced bonus requires at least 21% low, 12% very low or 15% moderate income units, or 100% affordable for the 75% bonus.
set.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 9, 2026: only readable source is the gocodebook mirror of County Code Chapter 17.12 (codepublishing.com 403; the County PLG-611 density bonus checklist opens but has no bonus terms), so confidence set to needs_confirmation under the mirror rule. Record omitted the very low, moderate and 100% affordable (75%) enhanced bonus tiers and the 30 units per acre cap, and tagged it homeownership only although it applies to rental projects.

reason: Material: record tagged the program homeownership only and omitted the 75% enhanced bonus for 100% affordable projects and the very low and moderate income tiers in Section 17.12.065.

set.typical_award_size: 823 PBVs in 33 developments as of February 2025 (El Centro 44, St. Stephens Senior 39, Water Street 33, Pippin Orchards 31, Resetar 52 and others) plus commitments to projects in development including Veterans Village (15). PBVs are awarded through a competitive RFP; the Fall 2024 RFP (open Oct 15 to Nov 18, 2024) offered up to 90 HCV and 15 VASH vouchers. HACSC planned two rounds a year timed to CTCAC, but the Spring-Summer 2025 RFP was cancelled because of federal funding uncertainty and no RFP has been reissued as of November 2026. Fall 2024 scoring: 200 base points (project type 45, HCV waiting list opportunities 25, poverty deconcentration 10, additional non-PBV affordable units 50, location 14, experience 6, readiness 15, community engagement 5, financial feasibility 30) plus up to 10 bonus points for supportive services or resident benefits; threshold 125 points for new construction and 120 for existing housing.
set.per_unit_cap: Project cap in the Fall 2024 RFP: the greater of 15 PBVs or 40% of total project units, with no exceptions. HACSC PBV Guidance (August 2026) says HUD permits project-basing up to 50% of authorized vouchers and up to 100% of units in a project, but HACSC may set lower limits for funding reasons.
set.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 9, 2026: RFP page confirms the cancelled Spring-Summer 2025 RFP, not in shortfall, interest list. October 2024 RFP scoring document and August 2026 PBV Guidance replace the prior scoring breakdown (threshold was listed as 150 with different category weights) and the prior caps (20% plus 10% and 24 CFR 983 income-mixing cap). The 823 PBV portfolio figure was not on these pages and was not rechecked.

reason: Material: record listed a 150-point threshold and a 24 CFR 983 income-mixing project cap, but the Fall 2024 RFP sets a 125-point new construction threshold and a project cap of the greater of 15 PBVs or 40% of units.

set.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 9, 2026: CDI page confirms HOME 2019 $700,000 TBRA, CDBG 2021 $500,000 street outreach, CDBG-CV $100,000, $348,000 and $350,000, CalHome mortgage assistance up to $56,400 not accepting applications, and the inactive manufactured home replacement program (up to $54,600). Prevailing wage true is uncited; federal HOME (12+ HOME units) and CDBG (8+ unit rehab) Davis-Bacon thresholds would apply only to development awards, which the County has not made.
